name: Upsell.com
summary: Shopify upsell app, formerly ReConvert: AI-driven cart, checkout and post-purchase upsell and cross-sell funnels, frequently-bought-together and product page recommendations, A/B testing and analytics with segmentation.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want one funnel covering product page, cart, post-purchase and thank-you offers with AI recommendations and A/B testing, and who sit under 500 orders a month, where the listing's Growth bands run from $9.99 to $39.99
skip_if: you are close to 2,000 orders a month, because the next rung is Scale at $299 a month and the vendor says it adds support rather than features, or you are not on Shopify Plus and were buying this for the checkout upsells, which stay closed to you
honest_knock: Growth is banded and cheap up to 500 orders, but the step after Growth is steep. The Shopify listing prints $9.99, $19.99 and $39.99 for the first three paid bands; the 1,000 and 2,000 bands are not in the served page. Past 2,000 orders a month, Scale costs $299 a month ($249 on annual) for a feature set the vendor says is identical on every plan; what it adds is priority chat, guided onboarding and earlier access to features. The pricing page also argues with itself twice: the Scale and Elite cards say billed monthly while the comparison table says annual only, and the annual toggle promises 25% off while the card prices work out at about 17%. Checkout upsells are still Shopify Plus only, so on a standard Shopify plan the checkout stage of the funnel stays shut.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Growth · per month for 51-100 monthly store orders or upsell revenue on the Shopify listing
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/reconvert-upsell-cross-sell and in our own test that day; earlier: prices re-verified 2026-11-09 on upsell.com/pricing in the Shopify view and on the Shopify App Store listing apps.shopify.com/reconvert-upsell-cross-sell the same day; this replaces the $199 Scale and $499 Elite rungs we recorded on 19 September) Billed in USD. The vendor's comparison still says "Every feature is included on every plan. Tiers differ by order volume and support", so you are buying volume and support, not features. Free covers up to 50 monthly store orders or upsell revenue, whichever is higher. Growth is priced by volume band up to 2,000. The Shopify listing prints the first three paid bands: $9.99 a month for 51-100, $19.99 for 101-200 and $39.99 for 201-500. The 1,000 and 2,000 bands sit behind a slider on upsell.com whose amounts are not in the served page, so we do not state them. Scale is $299 a month billed monthly, or $249 a month on the annual toggle, up to 10,000. Elite is $899 a month, or $749 on annual, up to 20,000. Enterprise is quote-only above 20,000 and adds one invoice across multiple stores. The page labels the annual toggle "Save 25% with Annual", but $249 against $299 and $749 against $899 both work out at about 17% off (our arithmetic). The page still disagrees with itself on billing: the Scale and Elite cards say "Billed monthly" while the comparison table lists both as "Annual only" and only Growth as "Monthly or annual". Both the pricing page and the listing offer a 14-day free trial. Checkout upsells remain for Shopify Plus stores only. Read again on 17 November 2026: the Shopify listing (ReConvert Post Purchase Upsell, developer Upsell.com ex ReConvert, 4.8 from 3,144 reviews) still shows Free for up to 50 orders or $50 of upsell revenue and the Growth bands at $9.99 (51 to 100), $19.99 (101 to 200) and $39.99 (201 to 500), each paid band with a 14 day trial. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store, installing the app did not open a plan list or a free plan: it went straight to Shopify's approval screen for a usage based subscription called Upsell.com, with an app spending limit of $2,000.00 per 30 days, a 14 day free trial ending 1 December, the line “You will not be billed for this test charge” and an Add payment method row. The screen said the app bills for usage when you begin to use it, and showed no $0 plan. We did not approve it, so we could not confirm how the free tier is applied.

Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-17.

compare_with.name: AfterSell
compare_with.why: Both cover the post-purchase and checkout upsell ground on Shopify. Upsell.com, formerly ReConvert, now lists its whole ladder on upsell.com/pricing, but only the first three Growth bands carry amounts in the served page ($9.99, $19.99 and $39.99, up to 500 orders, on the Shopify listing), and the step past 2,000 orders is to $299 a month. Compare the two on the order volume you expect in a year, not on today's.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed Upsell.com (ReConvert Post Purchase Upsell on the listing) on a Shopify development store. Straight after the install, before the app opened, Shopify showed an approval screen for usage charges up to $2.000,00 per 30 days that said there would be no charge for this test but also had an Add payment method row, so it was not approved and no upsell was set up. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid. Install: the listing was read at about 22:57 and the app was installed at about 22:57 in our own tab; the dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. After installing the screen said Installing Upsell.com... with a button Take me to the app, and then at about 22:58 the Shopify screen Approve subscription came up. The app itself did not open. Core action NOT DONE: the app did not open, because the subscription had to be approved first and the approval screen had an Add payment method row. No upsell was set up and no editor, preview, A/B test or setting was seen. Checkout: the screen Approve subscription showed the line You will not be billed for this test charge, Upsell.com ex ReConvert, This app bills you for usage charges, plan Upsell.com, an app spending limit of at most $2.000,00 USD per 30 days that can be updated after approval, a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec, You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it, and a row Add payment method. Our rule is to approve nothing on a screen with an Add payment method row, so nothing was approved and no card was entered. The screen showed no $0 plan and no plan list with amounts. Difference with the listing: the listing names a Free plan up to 50 orders and Growth plans from $9.99, while Shopify asked to approve usage charges up to $2.000,00 per 30 days. Cancelling: nothing was approved. The app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps, Uninstall with the reason Testing multiple apps. Clean up: the app is gone from Installed; no theme change and no order. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app does not open before a usage subscription is approved; the approval screen said there would be no charge for this test but still showed an Add payment method row, and it showed a spending limit of $2.000,00 per 30 days and no free plan.
